findings.title: AutoClip creators get generic clips from silent footage instead of a transcript failure — empty transcripts trigger evenly spaced placeholder cuts
findings.observed: Silent masters produce clips with score 40 and 'Lihat momen ini', without transcript analysis.

findings.title: AutoClip creators cannot analyze their YouTube reference's transcript or timestamps — ingestion fetches only oEmbed metadata and transcribes the uploaded master
findings.observed: YouTube reference contributes only title and author; its transcript and timestamps are never fetched.

findings.title: Creators can unknowingly publish Facebook or Instagram Reels publicly despite choosing private visibility — both platform executors ignore the approved visibility
findings.observed: Facebook always sends video_state=PUBLISHED; Instagram never applies the requested visibility.

findings.title: Creators see unpublished Instagram or TikTok videos marked published — the scheduler treats an unverified publish initiation as final success
findings.observed: Instagram error responses and TikTok pending publish IDs are stored as status 'terbit'.

findings.title: Creators cannot reliably erase deleted projects or their videos — project deletion only flags the parent while video and signed media endpoints remain accessible
findings.observed: Deleted project's video records and previously issued signed media URLs remain accessible.

findings.title: AutoClip crops can lose a moving speaker — six face samples are collapsed to one median position and rendered as a fixed crop
findings.observed: A subject moving across the frame gets one fixed crop_x for the entire clip.

findings.title: A revoked or superseded video can still be published — scheduled execution never rechecks the version's approval after scheduling
findings.observed: Unapproving a scheduled version does not stop its later upload.

findings.title: Creators can accidentally publish an old final while its replacement is being revised — starting a revision retains approved_version and publishing stays enabled
findings.observed: A revising video still exposes its old approved version to the publish dialog.

findings.title: Creators reviewing an old version see and export the latest version's captions and plan — revision overwrites video-level metadata and plan instead of versioning them
findings.observed: Selecting v1 after v2 displays and exports v2 metadata and plan.

findings.title: Creators can send a scheduled post immediately instead of at the requested future time — past dates are accepted and the scheduler immediately claims them
findings.observed: A past scheduled_at is stored as terjadwal and is eligible for immediate upload.

findings.title: Creators may post to the wrong Facebook or Instagram account — OAuth silently chooses the first returned Page rather than letting them select an account
findings.observed: A Meta login with multiple Pages connects pages[0] without an account selector.

findings.title: Keyboard-only creators cannot upload footage or a master file — the upload drop zone is a clickable non-focusable div and the file input is hidden
findings.observed: The file picker trigger cannot receive keyboard focus or be activated with Enter.

findings.title: Creators cannot produce or store videos with the supplied configuration — the storage and AI calls require a provider key absent from backend .env
findings.observed: The supplied backend .env does not define EMERGENT_LLM_KEY for storage or AI calls.
findings.notes: An externally injected process environment could supply it; that deployment configuration is not readable in the repository.

findings.title: Explainer creators can receive invented research presented as factual video content — custom-topic research uses GPT alone without fetching or grounding any source
findings.observed: Custom-topic research is generated from the topic alone with suggested, unverified sources.

findings.title: Creators can receive invalid editorial scores or seek outside the video — model output is stored unchecked and scored before the rendered video exists
findings.observed: Model scores and timestamp suggestions are stored without range, type, or duration validation.

findings.title: Creators cannot finish visual-only Explainer scene revisions — rebuilding scenes drops their durations but unchanged audio prevents recalculation
findings.observed: A visual-only Explainer scene edit drops scene dur and render fails with KeyError.

findings.title: AutoClip retries can produce duplicated clips and exceed the requested count — analysis inserts videos before its stage is marked done and retry runs the insertion again
findings.observed: Retrying an interrupted analyze stage inserts additional clips without removing partial clips.

findings.title: Creators can receive duplicate videos, versions and provider charges when multiple server instances start — every in-process worker requeues and executes the same jobs without a shared claim
findings.observed: Each server startup requeues all processing projects without an atomic worker claim.

findings.title: Concurrent review actions can queue overlapping revisions and produce duplicate version numbers — approve and unapprove overwrite the revising status without a transition guard
findings.observed: Approve and unapprove accept a video in revising state and overwrite its status.

findings.title: Large uploads can exhaust the server's memory and interrupt video production — the upload size limit is enforced only after reading the entire request
findings.observed: Files larger than 500 MB are fully read into RAM before the limit is checked.

findings.title: The studio can run out of disk space as creators upload and review videos — the local media cache never evicts even deleted or large assets
findings.observed: Every accessed master and output is copied to /tmp/luma/cache without eviction.

findings.title: Creators can accidentally post duplicate videos after an ambiguous upload failure — the scheduler frees the duplicate key without reconciling provider state
findings.observed: A timeout after provider acceptance marks the upload failed and clears the duplicate key.

findings.title: A creator can compromise another user's studio session through a shared media link — uploads trust the client content type and serve active HTML inline on the application origin
findings.observed: An uploaded .mp4 with text/html content type is served inline from the API origin.

findings.title: A scheduled video can be published to a different account than the creator approved — execution reloads the current channel after reconnect instead of binding the approved account
findings.observed: A scheduled post uses the currently connected account, not the one approved at scheduling.

findings.title: A malicious website can read a creator's private studio data if the browser sends their session cookie — credentialed CORS permits every origin
findings.observed: CORS allows every origin with credentials and the API accepts the session cookie.

findings.title: Creators can receive duplicate revision jobs and version numbers from concurrent requests — revision checks status and updates it in separate operations
findings.observed: Two concurrent revise requests can both see review status and enqueue a revision.

findings.title: Creators can see an archived project's video published later — project deletion neither cancels schedules nor blocks the scheduler from loading its videos
findings.observed: Archiving a project does not cancel its scheduled publications.

findings.title: Creators can be stuck indefinitely waiting for production when an AI call stalls — model, image, voice and transcription calls have no deadline or cancellation path
findings.observed: GPT, image, speech and transcription awaits have no application-level deadline.

findings.title: Creators can receive completed videos without the promised motion plan or platform captions — a valid but incomplete GPT JSON object is accepted as a successful plan
findings.observed: An AutoMotion GPT reply of {} still creates and renders a video with empty metadata.

findings.title: Creators do not see a newly revised video in the review queue — the revision keeps the old approved_version and the queue filters out all approved videos
findings.observed: After an approved video is revised, status is review but approved_version stays set.

findings.title: Creators cannot save a Brand Kit font or logo — the API model and renderer only support colors and a text watermark
findings.observed: PUT /api/brand-kit has no font or logo fields; rendered fonts are hardcoded.

findings.title: Creators cannot audit or label the generated music simulation — procedural audio is mixed into the MP4 and discarded without a simulation flag
findings.observed: Procedural music has no stored track or simulated flag in the project response.

findings.title: Creators cannot access older projects after the first 100 or search by title — the project API truncates the list and the page has no pagination or search
findings.observed: GET /api/projects returns at most 100 projects and ignores q.

findings.title: Creators lose the selected review version when they reload or share its URL — version selection lives only in component state
findings.observed: Reloading after selecting v1 returns to the latest version.

findings.title: Creators cannot copy a platform caption and hashtags in one action — the metadata editor has no copy control
findings.observed: Metadata tabs show fields and Save only; no copy action is present.

findings.title: Creators lose publication status and cannot retry after a server restart during upload — claimed sending jobs are never recovered or reconciled
findings.observed: A restart during an upload leaves status 'mengirim' permanently; the scheduler only scans 'terjadwal'.

findings.title: Creators cannot publish a newly approved revision to the same channel — the duplicate key omits the video version
findings.observed: A published v1 blocks scheduling v2 for the same channel with HTTP 409.

findings.title: Creators can save invalid project inputs and get failed or empty jobs — the project input is an unconstrained dictionary and URL validation only checks a substring
findings.observed: Project input accepts whitespace topics, invalid YouTube URLs, and arbitrary clip limits.

findings.title: Creators waste time on invalid video uploads that only fail during production — the upload endpoint checks the extension but not file contents or minimum size
findings.observed: A zero-byte or non-video file named .mp4 is accepted and stored as a master.

findings.title: A transient network failure leaves creators stuck on the project error screen — successful progress polls never clear the previous error
findings.observed: After one failed poll, setErr stays set even when later project reads succeed.

findings.title: Creators mistake failed dashboard and library requests for empty data or blank pages — load handlers silently discard network and API errors
findings.observed: Failed list and Brand Kit requests are swallowed, leaving empty or blank screens.

findings.title: A copied session token remains usable after its owner signs out — API authorization never checks the Clerk session's revocation status
findings.observed: A signed-out session's unexpired JWT is accepted based only on its signature and claims.

findings.title: Creators cannot clear their Brand Kit CTA or tone — reads replace saved empty strings with defaults
findings.observed: Saving an empty CTA or tone reads back the default instead of the saved empty value.

findings.title: Creators' saved Brand Kit narration voice is ignored for new Explainers — the wizard always submits its hardcoded warm-voice default
findings.observed: The wizard always sends voice='hangat', overriding a saved cinematic Brand Kit voice.

findings.title: Creators miss older videos awaiting review and see an understated queue count — the queue silently caps both projects and videos
findings.observed: The review queue stops at 30 videos and only considers the first 500 projects.

findings.title: Creators lose caption edits while a revision runs — each poll replaces the metadata object and the editor resets its local draft
findings.observed: Polling during a revision replaces unsaved metadata edits every 3 seconds.

findings.title: Creators cannot identify the master or footage attached to a reloaded project — project detail omits the source asset's original filename and size
findings.observed: The project detail returns an asset ID and probe data, but no source filename or size.

findings.title: Creators cannot open the specified project library or review deep links — the router only defines /proyek paths and redirects /projects to the dashboard
findings.observed: Opening /projects or /projects/{id} falls through to the dashboard redirect.

findings.title: Phone and keyboard users cannot discover the project archive control — its icon appears only on pointer hover
findings.observed: The project archive button is opacity-0 unless its card is hovered.

findings.title: Creators cannot publish to pull-URL platforms when a media host is configured — the publisher prefixes an already absolute signed URL with the app host
findings.observed: An absolute PUBLIC_MEDIA_BASE is concatenated after PUBLIC_APP_URL when publishing.

findings.title: Creators outside WIB can schedule a post for the wrong intended time — the schedule input is interpreted in the browser zone without a zone label while status is displayed in WIB
findings.observed: datetime-local is interpreted in the browser's local zone, then the publication list shows WIB.

findings.title: Creators cannot inspect which transcript and timestamps AutoClip used — project detail strips the saved transcript and exposes only a word count
findings.observed: Project detail returns transcript_words count but excludes the transcript and timestamps.

findings.title: Explainer production progress moves backward after the first image — the reference-scene and remaining-scene batches reset the visual stage's progress counter
findings.observed: Explainer visual-stage progress goes from 100% for scene 1 to 20% for scene 2 of 5.

findings.title: Creators cannot use Ide Hari Ini during a trends and GPT outage — evergreen fallback also depends on the failed GPT service
findings.observed: When both trend feeds and GPT fail, /api/trends errors and the ideas panel is blank.

findings.title: Creators see raw provider and ffmpeg diagnostics instead of actionable errors — job and publication failures persist unfiltered internal exception text
findings.observed: Provider and ffmpeg exception strings are stored and displayed directly to users.

findings.title: Creators' review queues slow as their video libraries grow — the user/status query sorts updated_at without a supporting compound index
findings.observed: Review queue lacks index (user_id, status, updated_at DESC) for its filtered sort.

findings.title: Filtering a large project library slows for creators — the user/mode/creation-time query has no matching compound index
findings.observed: Mode filter lacks index (user_id, mode, created_at DESC).

findings.title: Creators can queue invalid revision instructions or time ranges — the revision model neither trims text nor validates timestamps against each other and the video duration
findings.observed: Revision accepts instruction='   ', negative start and end before start.

findings.title: Creators can accidentally erase generated platform captions — metadata save replaces the entire dictionary without requiring the four platform records or nonempty fields
findings.observed: Saving metadata can replace all four platform entries with an empty dictionary.

findings.title: Creators get a silent failed player or download after a media link expires — review never handles media errors or refreshes its six-hour signed URLs
findings.observed: The video element has no error handler for broken or expired signed media URLs.

findings.title: Project thumbnails disappear from a large library even when their videos exist — asset_map truncates the combined asset lookup at 500 entries
findings.observed: asset_map loads at most 500 assets, including every Explainer scene image.

findings.title: Creators cannot correct a project's source or settings without making a new project — sources are accepted only at creation and no edit or source-attachment route exists
findings.observed: No project-source or settings edit endpoint or review control exists.

findings.title: API creators cannot start Ide Hari Ini by choosing only a style — project creation requires a supplied idea instead of applying the stored AI recommendation
findings.observed: Creating a trend Explainer without an idea returns 400 rather than selecting recommended.

findings.title: Creators with non-Latin video titles can fail to download their MP4 — the raw Unicode filename is interpolated into a Latin-1 HTTP header
findings.observed: A non-Latin video title can reach a Content-Disposition header that cannot encode it.

findings.title: Creators receive no explanation when channel loading, undo approval or retry fails — these asynchronous controls discard or leave request errors unhandled
findings.observed: Failed channel loading, unapprove or retry requests have no visible error handler.

findings.title: Creators are shown US-only search trends as global trends — the Global feed is hardcoded to the United States
findings.observed: Ideas labeled Global come from Google Trends geo=US only.

findings.title: Creators cannot browse each finished clip in the dashboard gallery — it displays one thumbnail per project rather than each produced video
findings.observed: A five-clip project contributes only one project thumbnail to the gallery.

findings.title: Creators cannot remove uploaded masters from their storage library — the asset deletion API has no frontend control
findings.observed: The source library lists masters but exposes no action to delete them.

findings.title: Creators can see stale or regressing job progress after a slow request — polling applies responses without checking their request order
findings.observed: Overlapping polls apply whichever response arrives last, including older snapshots.

findings.title: Creators cannot select older stored masters once their library exceeds 200 files — the asset endpoint silently truncates results and the picker has no pages
findings.observed: The source picker only loads the newest 200 uploaded masters with no pagination.

findings.title: Creators' connected Meta and TikTok channels stop publishing when their tokens expire — their refresh tokens and expiry are never handled
findings.observed: Only YouTube refreshes tokens; Meta and TikTok tokens are never refreshed.

findings.title: Creators can see a channel marked connected despite a failed account lookup — OAuth swallows the provider error and stores an unverified connection
findings.observed: An account lookup error still sets connected=true with account_name=null.

findings.title: Creators cannot review an Explainer's research after production finishes — the research panel is rendered only inside the processing or failed state
findings.observed: The research panel disappears as soon as the Explainer enters review status.

findings.title: Creators can see no usable or recommended trend ideas after a malformed GPT reply — trend results are stored without checking nonempty ideas or a valid best index
findings.observed: An empty ideas list or negative best index yields no recommended trend idea.

findings_minor.title: An unapproved video retains its previous approval timestamp — the unapprove transition does not clear approved_at
findings_minor.observed: Unapprove clears approved_version but retains approved_at from the previous approval.

findings_minor.title: A malformed media seek request fails with an internal server error — the Range parser converts unvalidated values to integers
findings_minor.observed: A malformed Range header causes int() to raise rather than returning HTTP 416.

findings_withdrawn.title: Explainer revisions can export subtitles from deleted scenes — scene removal does not invalidate the existing voice transcript and timed words
findings_withdrawn.reason: Removing a scene with all remaining audio unchanged first fails rendering because scene durations were dropped; no new version is exported. Covered by R-BUG-021.
